They ought to consider, that our Saviour did truly Judge, they deserved no Answer, for his Works had testified of him, that he acted by a Divine Power; he should not need tell them so, in so many Words, 2. In very deed, there was a direct Answer couched in this Question of our Saviour. I pray, saith he, by what Authority did <ns0:hi>Iohn Preach and Bap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tize?</ns0:hi> They could not say by an <ns0:hi>Humane Authority,</ns0:hi> for they knew he was not Licensed by their <ns0:hi>Masters</ns0:hi>: It must follow that he Acted by Vertue of an extraordinary Divine Mission, so do I (saith our Saviour) and have given you a greater Proof of it, than ever <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptist did.</ns0:hi> But our Lord well knew, that the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had a greater Reverence for <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> than for him, and that many of the People had a great Opinion of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> indeed greater than of him, our Saviour <ns0:hi>coming Eating and Drinking,</ns0:hi> as he ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />presseth it, (that is) being of a more free, and sociable Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />versation, which did not to please the Pharasaical, morose, and supercilious Humour; he therefore chuseth to teach them by a Question, in which assoon as they could resolve themselves, they might know by what Authority he did, what he did. Besides, by the <ns0:hi>Baptism of Iohn,</ns0:hi> mentioned in our Saviours. Question, is not to be understood only his Administration of <ns0:hi>Baptism,</ns0:hi> but his <ns0:hi>Doctrine,</ns0:hi> and indeed the whole of his Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nistery: For as his Baptism, is called the <ns0:hi>Baptism of Repen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />

                        </ns0:gap>ance</ns0:hi>; so the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> here argue, that if they should say <ns0:hi>from Heaven,</ns0:hi> He <ns0:hi>would</ns0:hi> say, <ns0:hi>why then did you not believe him,</ns0:hi> which must be understood of his <ns0:hi>Doctrine</ns0:hi>: A great part of <ns0:hi>Iohns Doctrine</ns0:hi> was, that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was come, that <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> was he, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.20. he pointed to him and said: <ns0:hi>Behold the L<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                        </ns0:gap>ssiah.</ns0:hi> But why did not they say <ns0:hi>of Men?</ns0:hi> The Text saith, <ns0:hi>They feared the Pe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

And the <ns0:hi>Publicans, and Harlots.</ns0:hi> Great sinners, bad and vile People, making no pretence to Religion: God saith to the one, and the other, <ns0:hi>Go and work in my Vineyard,</ns0:hi> that is, do my Will. Do the Work I command you to do. Others, by their Lives declare, <ns0:hi>That they will not go.</ns0:hi> But yet upon se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cond Thoughts, having their Hearts touched by the Finger of God, they do Gods work, <ns0:hi>Which of them did the Will of his Father? They say to him the first.</ns0:hi> This is plain, for what was the Will of the <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> but that they should do the Work he set them to do? This the latter did not; the Fathers Will was not only that the Son should give him a Cap, and a Knee, and Complement him, but that he should go to work in the Vineyard<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> It is the least part of Gods Will, that Men should give him good Words be a little Complemental, and Ceremonious to<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

This, some <ns0:hi>Publicans and Harlots</ns0:hi> did, the Generality of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> refused. It is an hard thing to convince a Moral, Righteous, Civil man, that he lacks any thing to Sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation; and hence it is that <ns0:hi>Profane</ns0:hi> Persons many times re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pent, believe and are saved, when others perish in their impeni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tency and unbelief, because they think, they have no need of <ns0:hi>Repentance,</ns0:hi> or any further <ns0:hi>Righteousness,</ns0:hi> than they are possessed of.</ns0:note>
